name: Question 3
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t),$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{4}{5}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{5}\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t))\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4(-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t))+C \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{4}{5}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & =\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot 0)+C \\ \frac{4}{5} & =\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+C \\ \frac{4}{5} & =\frac{4}{5}\cdot 1+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{5}\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{5}) & =\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\cdot (-1) \\  & =-\frac{4}{5} \\  & =-0.8\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $0.8\,\text{m/s}.$

Question 3
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=−4sin⁡(5t), where a(t) is measured in m/s2 and t is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=45m/s when t=0s, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment t=π5s.

a
0.6m/s
b
0.625m/s2
c
0.8m/s
d
1.25m/s2
e
1m/s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(−4sin⁡(5t))dt=−4(−15cos⁡(5t))+C=45cos⁡(5t)+C. To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=45. Substituting this into the above gives 45=45cos⁡(5⋅0)+C45=45cos⁡(0)+C45=45⋅1+CC=0. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=45cos⁡(5t).

We evaluate the velocity at time t=π5s: v(π5)=45cos⁡(5⋅π5)=45cos⁡(π)=45⋅(−1)=−45=−0.8m/s.

Finally, since the speed is equal to |v(t)|, we conclude that the speed of the particle is 0.8m/s.
